source_text:
Hymnus
ΓΕΩΡΓΙΟΙΟ ΑΛΙΤΡΟΙΟ ΥΜΝΟΣ
Μνώεο, Χριστέ, υἱὲ θεοῖο ὑψιμέδοντος, οἰκέτεω σέο κῆρ' ἀλιτροῖο γράψαντος
τάδε· καί μοι ὄπασσον λῦσιν παθέων κηριτρεφέων, τά μοι ἐμφύει ψυχᾷ ῥυπαρᾷ· δὸς
δὲ ἰδέσθαι, σῶτερ Ἰησοῦ, ζαθέαν αἴγλαν σάν· ἔνθα φανεὶς μέλψω ἀοιδὰν ψυχᾶν
παίονι, παίονι γυίων πατρὶ σὺν μεγάλῳ πνεύματι θ' ἁγνῷ.
orientation: The poet Georgius, speaking as a sinner, prays to Christ for release from inner passions and for the sight of Christ's holy radiance so that he may sing a healing song to the Father and the Holy Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, your servant's heart, a sinner's, having written these things; and grant me release from heart-bred passions, which grow in my impure soul; and grant me to see, Savior Jesus, your holy radiance; there appearing I may sing a song healing for souls, healing for limbs, to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.

choices.why: The glossary decided form is 'most high', matching the brief's fixed rendering for this epithet of God the Father.
The glossary fixed rendering for the poet's self-description; 'sinner' preserves the noun force of the Greek adjective used substantivally.
The glossary fixed rendering; 'heart-bred' keeps the compound's literal sense of being nourished in the heart.
The glossary fixed rendering; 'impure' conveys the defilement needing cleansing.
The glossary fixed rendering; 'radiance' captures the light's shining quality.
The glossary fixed rendering; 'song' is neutral and fits the metrical context.

pass_b_english: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, your servant's heart—a sinner's heart—that has written these lines. Grant me release from the heart-bred passions growing in my impure soul. And grant me, Savior Jesus, to see your holy radiance, so that, appearing in that light, I may sing a healing song for souls and limbs to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.

problems.why: Intro uses different epithet than all hymn sections.

problems.quote: the heart of your servant, a sinner
problems.why: Different phrasing of same self-description across versions.
problems.fix: Flag as manuscript variants, not different content.

variants.text: the heart of your servant, a sinner

problems.quote: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, the heart of your servant
problems.why: The opening line is restructured across sections; a reader comparing them may think the meaning shifted.
problems.fix: Use one consistent rendering across all sections or label them as deliberate variants.

fixed: The English already uses 'most high God' in the opening line, matching the source and the glossary decision.
The English already renders the self-description as 'your servant's heart—a sinner's heart', which matches the source's 'your servant's heart, a sinner's'.
The opening line is restructured in the English for naturalness, but the meaning is unchanged; no edit needed beyond the gloss alignment.
